fr3181-f55.summary: The thirteen ciphered lines of Catherine de Médicis's letter to the bishop of Rennes that La Ferrière printed as 'Partie chiffrée': the Council of Trent and the Habsburg marriage ('avancer le concile', 'pour le bien de la Chrestienté', the December sessions).

c390-p357.summary: The precedence dispute at the imperial court after Ferdinand I's death (1564): another pretext must be found than the one in the sieur Charon's despatch, and a secretary or one of Rennes's people be left there under colour of private business.

c390-p139.summary: A secret note from Catherine: decipher it yourself, trust no clerk, burn it; she holds Rennes a loyal servant of the King her son and asks him to keep his eyes open to observe 'mon cousin' and his actions. The least-read of the four (about 70% strict sense).

c392-p231.summary: Bourdin encloses Catherine's letter of 15 Dec 1562 on the secret marriage overture; its leak to Spain ('sçavoit incontinant en Espaigne'), the triumph over 'la premiere ouverture ... de ce mariage', closing on friendship and alliance for the repose of Christendom.

fr3181-f55-v3.summary: The thirteen cipher lines that La Ferrière printed blank: Catherine agrees with what Rennes has found out about the marriage[s] and with his advice on them; someone put forward to him a plan for the good of Christendom and to advance the Council of Trent; each party pursues its own design; the benefit of the Council and of the December sessions is still to be seen.

system: Homophonic substitution on invented signs, two to eight per letter, with about thirty word-signs and a set of nulls that includes ordinary French words written in clear.
